xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-3668: Add Prime Agent as a managed harness

plan.title: Add Prime Agent as a managed harness
plan.author: agent:k3[1m]

narratives.Problem: Overdeck cannot launch or supervise Prime Agent as a harness. Prime Agent publishes a persistent JSONL RPC mode (prompt, steer, follow_up, abort, get_state, get_messages, get_session_stats) plus durable sessions, but Overdeck has no canonical literal, behavior record, transport, runtime adapter, delivery mapping, transcript adapter, cost projection, context rendering, or dashboard support for it. A shallow integration would leave gaps in delivery, recovery, costs, transcripts, context, and dashboard status.
narratives.Proposal: Full managed-harness parity per the canonical PRD (drafts/pan-3668.md on overdeck-state): add the prime-agent literal and PRIME_AGENT_BEHAVIOR to contracts; a strict LF-delimited JSONL framing module plus a persistent RPC client (never Node readline — U+2028/U+2029 are valid JSON string content); a registered runtime adapter with verified session resume; work/conversation launch and prompt/steer/follow_up delivery mapping; transcript, cost, health, and dashboard projections; a prime-agent-global.md context artifact injected at spawn without touching ~/.prime/agent; doctor diagnostics and table-driven provider mapping; a mechanical no-loss audit; and full operator documentation. Cloister remains the only lifecycle authority: Prime schedules, heartbeats, autonomous continuation, cross-agent messaging, and retained RLM children are disabled by injected policy and adapter-side rejection, with a conversations-only fallback if the pinned release cannot enforce this.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Training or evaluating models through Prime Intellect Lab or verifiers
- Installing or managing Prime Intellect GPU compute
- Importing Prime Agent continual-harness refinements into bundled, machine, project, or workspace context layers
- Exposing Prime schedules, autonomous mode, or heartbeat scheduling as Overdeck pipeline controls in the first release
- Treating Prime worker and kernel processes as a security sandbox
- Registering arbitrary Prime RLM children as first-class Overdeck work agents in the first release
- Adding a hardcoded default model or changing existing provider-to-harness defaults

autoDecisions.summary: Used the canonical PRD at drafts/pan-3668.md verbatim instead of authoring a new one
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue comment names it implementation-ready; every code reference in it re-verified against the codebase on 2026-08-12, so rewriting would add risk, not information.

autoDecisions.summary: One xBRIEF with plan.metadata.sizeJustification instead of sibling-issue decomposition
autoDecisions.rationale: The operator scoped this as a single issue with a single PRD; no intermediate slice passes review/test/UAT independently because the acceptance criteria are end-to-end (select, message, observe, stop, recover).

autoDecisions.summary: Split the RPC transport into a pure framing module and a stateful client
autoDecisions.rationale: Pure LF framing is exhaustively unit-testable without a process, and the split keeps the inspection-worthy stateful client small.

autoDecisions.summary: Recorded the conversations-only fallback as a decision/hazard instead of asking the operator
autoDecisions.rationale: The PRD already prescribes exactly this fallback when the pinned Prime release cannot mechanically disable autonomous features; auto mode must choose documented defaults.

autoDecisions.summary: Scheduled the no-loss audit near the end of the DAG
autoDecisions.rationale: The audit asserts the finished harness-facing surface; landing it early would force it to assert a surface that does not exist yet.

metadata.sizeJustification: Single coherent harness integration scoped by the operator as one issue with one implementation-ready PRD (drafts/pan-3668.md). Every slice depends on the canonical literal/behavior contract and the RPC transport, and the issue acceptance criteria (operator can select, message, observe, stop, and recover a Prime session) only hold end-to-end — intermediate slices such as contracts-only or transport-only ship dead code that cannot pass review/test/UAT on their own.

Implement strict LF-delimited JSONL framing for the Prime RPC protocol

expected_outputs: framing tests pass for U+2028/U+2029 payloads, CRLF, split records, combined records, oversized records, and malformed JSON

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/prime-agent/jsonl-framing.ts as a pure, incremental byte-buffer framing module: split only on LF (never Node readline — Prime documents U+2028/U+2029 as valid JSON string content), strip one trailing CR before JSON.parse, reject records over a named size bound with a typed error, and isolate malformed JSON to a per-record error without killing the stream. Expose a push(chunk) → records/errors API. Tests must cover U+2028 and U+2029 inside JSON strings, CRLF input, records split across chunks, multiple records in one chunk, oversized records, and malformed JSON.

items.title: The framer preserves U+2028 and U+2029 inside JSON strings and returns the record intact as one record
